title: Cofinal quotient reductions preserve constructibility and uniform Tor bounds
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $O$ and uniformizer $\pi$, and a scheme $T$. Put $R=\mathcal O_{E,T}$, $B_N=(O/\ell^N)_T$ and $D_j=(O/\pi^j)_T$ for $N,j\geq1$ [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers]. Write $\ell=u\pi^e$ with $u\in O^\times$ and $e\geq1$. For $K\in D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and $eN\geq j$, the canonical quotient $B_N\to D_j$ induces a natural scalar-associativity isomorphism in $D(D_j)$
$$\bigl(K\otimes_R^LB_N\bigr)\otimes_{B_N}^LD_j\xrightarrow{\sim}K\otimes_R^LD_j,$$
where all tensors are the target-coefficient derived change of rings of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. If $P\to K$ is a K-flat resolution with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex], then $P\otimes_RB_N$ is K-flat over $B_N$ and this isomorphism is represented by the ordinary reassociation map to $P\otimes_RD_j$, with its $D_j$-action. The comparisons are natural in $K$ and commute with further quotient maps in both indices.

Suppose there are integers $a\leq b$ such that for every $N\geq1$ the complex $K\otimes_R^LB_N$ has constructible cohomology [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] and Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Then for every $j\geq1$, $K\otimes_R^LD_j$ has constructible cohomology and Tor amplitude in the same $[a,b]$; in particular all its cohomology sheaves outside $[a,b]$ vanish. This applies to arbitrary ramification index $e$ and arbitrary $T$; it requires no flatness or finite projective dimension of $D_j$ over $B_N$, no invertibility of $\ell$ on $T$, and no completeness assumption on $K$.

proof.text: Fix j and choose N=j; positivity e>=1 gives j+1<=e*(j+1). Compare the quantified quotient presentation with the canonical scalarExtensionFunctor: its object/map equations give an ordinary natural isomorphism to reductionChange, which lifts to homotopy categories; uniqueness of universal left derived functors gives the derived natural isomorphism. Compose its inverse with n.derived and the coefficient equality to identify canonical extension of the jth ell reduction with the jth uniformizer reduction. The cocone gives annihilation of both finite rings by ell^(j+1). The input Tor bound supplies bounded cohomological support through the already proved scalar-extension flat-model helper. Apply scalarExtensionFunctor_preserves_constructible_tor with these actual finite rings. Transport constructibility through each cohomology isomorphism using the existing constructible-isomorphism helper; transport Tor amplitude through the bounded flat model. That same flat model has zero terms outside [a,b], hence zero cohomology there. The proof uses no flatness of the quotient, no completeness of K and no invertibility assumption on the scheme.
